about.title: What is HeartEats
about.intro: HeartEats is a map of places to eat in Madrid where people with disabilities work. It is meant to help you choose calmly where to go, knowing who is behind it.

sections.heading: Why it exists
paragraphs: Going out to eat is something we all do every day. We like the idea that choosing a place where people with disabilities work can be as simple as any other choice, and that it is chosen for what really matters: tasty food, kind service and a good job.

sections.heading: What you will find here
items: Places with real inclusive employment: what counts is who works there.
Independent businesses and projects with social impact, which are the ones that need visibility most and the ones we can get to know closely.
If you are looking for information about ramps or adapted toilets, other tools exist for that. HeartEats is not a job board either.

sections.heading: How it works
items: Anyone can suggest a place or a correction.
A person reviews each suggestion calmly before it is published.
The business always has the final word: nobody appears on the map without knowing.
Each listing tells you how and when its details were checked.

sections.heading: The people on the team
paragraphs: Each listing talks about the team as a whole. A person’s name, photo or story only appears if they decide so themselves and give their permission, and they can change their mind whenever they like.

sections.heading: Open and non-profit
paragraphs: HeartEats is a non-profit project. Its code is open (AGPL-3.0 licence) and so is the business database (ODbL licence). People’s stories, names and photos are outside that licence. The map relies on open data and always shows where it comes from.

sections.heading: Where we are
paragraphs: We are starting in Madrid, hoping to reach more cities little by little. HeartEats is being built: for now you will see example places, which do not exist and are marked as [DEMO].

verification.title: How we verify
verification.intro: We want every point on the map to be trustworthy. That is why nothing is published until a person has reviewed it and the business itself agrees.

sections.heading: What happens when someone suggests a place
items: We receive the suggestion. It is not public yet.
An automatic filter helps us avoid unwanted messages and recognise places that were already on the map.

A person calmly checks that the place exists, that it is independent and that its team is inclusive. They rely on a link, news, the business’s website, agreements or references from organisations in the sector.

We get in touch with the business through an official channel. We would like to know whether it is happy to appear, and to offer it the chance to tell its team’s story at the level of detail it prefers.
With all of this a decision is made: it is published, we ask for a little more information or, if it does not fit, we explain why. Everything is noted down.

sections.heading: What each level means
paragraphs: Places that have not been checked yet do not appear on the map.
items: Verified details: our team has checked them with a visit, a call or documents.
Details confirmed by the community: confirmed by the business itself with some proof, or by several people who do not know each other.

sections.heading: How we check
paragraphs: We use these methods, from strongest to weakest:
items: A visit to the place.
Direct confirmation from the business, by phone or by email from its official domain.
Documents: agreements, certifications or official statements.
References from organisations in the sector.

sections.heading: Which businesses fit
paragraphs: HeartEats focuses on independent businesses and projects with social impact, because they are the ones that need visibility most and the ones we can get to know closely. Large chains and corporate franchises are not part of this map. This is not a judgement of their work or of the people who work there: it is simply the focus we have chosen.
If you are unsure about a case, such as a co-operative, a small group or a social project with several places, tell us: we will look at it calmly, one by one.

sections.heading: Keeping details up to date
items: Each listing shows the level, the method and the date of the last check.
After 12 months, the listing is marked to be reviewed again.
Anyone can suggest a correction or ask for a listing to be removed.
The business can ask for changes or to leave whenever it likes.

sections.heading: We look after your privacy when reviewing
paragraphs: Suggestions from other people do not include details about those on the team. If someone writes them, we leave them out when reviewing. The email of the person who suggests is private, and we only use it in case we need to ask them something.

privacy.title: Privacy and data
privacy.intro: This text is a draft: a professional still has to review it and it may change before launch. It is written in plain language, for people who are not lawyers.

sections.heading: In short
items: You can use HeartEats without giving us any data: there are no accounts, we do not use our own cookies and we do not measure your activity.
If you suggest a place or a correction, you tell us what you want about the place. Your email is optional, private, and only used in case we need to ask you something.
We do not publish or keep names or health data of people without their express permission. If someone writes them in a suggestion, we leave them out when we review it.
If a business decides to tell its team story, the business does it, and each person gives their consent. They can withdraw it whenever they want, without giving reasons.

sections.heading: This version is a test
paragraphs: Right now, sending suggestions, corrections and business forms is a simulation: nothing is saved. What follows describes how we will handle data once sending is real.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for the data
paragraphs: Until an association exists, the person responsible is the person behind the project: Marlon Bermúdez, in a personal capacity. When the association is set up, this section will change. How to write to us is on the Contact page.

sections.heading: What data we handle and why
items: If you use the website: none of our own. The web server and the map server see your IP address when they serve you the page, like any server.
If you tap Near me: your location is used only on your device, to sort places by distance. It is not sent or saved, and it is only requested when you tap the button.

If you suggest a place: the place details, how you know it, a link (optional) and your email (optional). We use them to review the suggestion and, if it meets the criteria, publish it. The suggestion is kept until it is resolved; your email is deleted when it is resolved or after 6 months at the most.

If you suggest a correction: what needs correcting, your explanation, a link (optional) and your email (optional). We use them to review the notice and, if it is right, update the listing. They are kept like a suggestion.
If you are a moderator: your email and the area you moderate, so you can sign in and review suggestions, for as long as you are one.
To prevent unwanted messages: a temporary counter per IP address, kept for a few hours. The hidden field in the form does not store anything about you.

If you are a business and tell your team story: team figures and, at the highest level, name or pseudonym, role, story and photo of each person, to show the listing with the detail the business chooses. They are kept for as long as the business and the person keep them.
paragraphs: We handle your email and what you write in the forms because you give them to us when you send them (your consent). The data of a team member is handled only with that person's explicit consent.

sections.heading: The people on the team
paragraphs: This section matters most to us, so we explain it in simple words.
items: A suggestion from someone else does not include data about team members. If someone writes names or health data, we leave them out when we review it.
Only the business can tell the story of its team, and never in detail without its knowledge. Until the business confirms, we only show public, verifiable information.
Each person decides for themselves whether to appear, under what name (it can be a pseudonym) and with what photo. Where it applies, their legal representative decides.
A story without recorded consent is not saved.
It can be withdrawn at any time, without giving reasons. The story stops being shown immediately and the data is deleted within 7 days at the most.

In small teams (fewer than 5 people) we make sure nobody can be recognised: we do not publish figures by type of disability or by role when they could identify someone, and we only give general figures.
Stories, names and photos are not under an open licence and are never included in open data exports.

sections.heading: Third parties involved
items: Website hosting: Netlify. It records the IP address of whoever visits the site, like any server.
Map: tiles and styles are served by OpenFreeMap. When you open the map, your browser requests them directly and they see your IP address. We send them nothing else.
Server and database: once it exists, we will state here the provider and the country where the data is stored.
We do not sell or share data with anyone.

sections.heading: Open data
paragraphs: The business database is published under the ODbL licence: name, address, type of cuisine, verification level and aggregate figures. It does not include stories, names, photos, emails or data about whoever suggests or corrects.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask us to access your data, correct it, delete it, limit its use, object to it or receive it in a portable format. If you gave us your consent, you can withdraw it at any time, and that does not affect what has already been handled. We will answer within one month at the most.
If you ever feel we have not looked after your data well, you can complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es). Before that, we would love the chance to sort it out with you.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: Data is kept on servers with restricted access and an encrypted connection. The email of whoever suggests or corrects is only seen by the moderation team.

sections.heading: Changes to this text
paragraphs: If something important changes, we will update it here and change the date. Version: draft, October 2026.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: There is a way for each thing. Almost everything can be done from the website itself.

sections.heading: Suggest a place or correct a detail
paragraphs: Anyone can do it, without an account. A person reviews it calmly before it is published.

sections.heading: If you run a business
paragraphs: Tell us about your team with the level of detail you prefer. You decide how much is told.

sections.heading: Withdraw a story or use your rights
paragraphs: To withdraw a story, a photo or a listing there is a form on the website: no account and no explanations needed. We write to the email you leave to confirm it is you.

For other rights over your data you will also have an email address. We are still setting it up and it will be ready before the project opens to the public. Until then, do not write personal data in a public channel.

sections.heading: Website bugs and code
paragraphs: HeartEats code is open. If you found a bug on the website, you can tell us on GitHub. It is a public site: please do not include personal data.
